compiled_state.title: Closure Checks schema migration: separate end-state intent from transitional work across all planning artifacts
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context

LLM sub-agents (brainstorm, preplanning, sprint task-execution, completion-verifier) treat every SC/DoD/AC item identically today, conflating durable system properties with one-time sprint achievements. Concrete failure modes: the completion verifier produces false-positive closures when transitional tasks masquerade as durable SCs; brainstorm authors write change-detector-style transitional items into SC sections that downstream test-generation systems then treat as test targets; the entire calibration program (d566-afa6, 94ed-f55c, 411b-a047, 7f42-e41f, 69e8-af39) is blocked until this distinction is structural. This epic delivers the schema cleavage as root prerequisite. Ships in four sequential phases — templates, verifier, audit, migration — with a multi-opus coherence walk-through gate before migration cutover.

## Success Criteria

- SC1: Epic/story/task templates (plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/phases/epic-description-template.md and equivalents in preplanning, implementation-plan) include "## Closure Checks" section after end-state sections. Required at epic level; optional at story/task with per-level granularity guidance in template comments.

- SC2: plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/verifiable-sc-check.md gains an end-state-only rule with canonical litmus test: "Could this item be false before the sprint began and true only because of this sprint's specific work? If yes, route to Closure Checks." Rule includes accept/reject example list covering past-tense durable invariants (accept: "the system supports OAuth"; accept: "the legacy adapter is absent from imports"; reject: "OAuth has been migrated"; reject: "legacy adapter has been removed"). Brainstorm refusal copy added: "This SC describes a one-time transition rather than a durable system property — moving it to Closure Checks. To keep it as an SC, reframe it as ongoing system behavior."

- SC3: plugins/dso/agents/completion-verifier.md refactored:
  (a) reads "## Closure Checks" separately from end-state items;
  (b) validates each Closure Check one-shot at closure;
  (c) walks descendant subtree via parent_id ONLY (not relates_to or depends_on, avoiding shared-descendant fan-out blocking); skips descendants in closed/deleted status; treats blocked as open unless all blockers terminal; emits WARN (not BLOCK) on open descendants without Closure Checks;
  (d) handles tickets without "## Closure Checks" section gracefully (treat as zero checks = pass, preserving legacy compatibility);
  (e) exposes end-state-item-validator hook at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/end-state-item-validator.md with contract_version=1, input={item_text, item_source_ticket_id, closure_timestamp}, output={valid: bool, reason: string, severity: "block"|"warn"}. Default validator returns {valid: true, severity: "warn"} on present and well-formed items. Contract document includes one worked example of a custom validator.

  Outcome: verifier no longer produces false-positive closures on tickets containing mixed Closure Check and SC items.

- SC4: plugins/dso/scripts/audit-closure-checks-migration.sh implements combined methodology over .md, .sh, .py, .yaml, .yml files in plugins/, tests/, docs/. Pattern sweep includes variable-interpolation hints (e.g., $VAR='Closure Checks'), aliases (closure-chk, cc-items), and section-name regex. Reverse-dependency enumeration follows static imports AND flags dynamic loads (importlib.import_module with variable, $PLUGIN_ROOT-rooted sourcing). Six classification buckets: section-name-reference, file-path-reference, semantic-consumer, test-asserting-on-structure, user-facing-copy, migration-in-progress. Output: structured JSON to plugins/dso/.audit-output/closure-checks-migration-<timestamp>.json. Reconciliation pass terminates after max 5 iterations with remaining flags surfaced as RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE.

- SC5: Pointer updates land per bucket recipe across consumer files identified by SC4. Re-running the audit script returns zero unflagged matches OR an explicit RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE block listing residuals (steady state).

- SC6: plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh dispatches a haiku classifier per SC/DoD/AC item on every brainstorm:complete-tagged epic. Classifier returns {label: end-state|transitional|uncertain, ranking: 1-5, rationale: string}. Escalate to user on label=uncertain OR ranking <= 3. Migration review batches capped at 25 items per batch; per-item explicit acknowledge required (no batch-approve button). Migration is snapshot-based and idempotent — re-runs pick up tickets edited during prior passes. Audit comment per ticket records {snapshot_timestamp, original_text, classification, ranking, rationale}.

- SC7: Synthetic end-to-end test. A /dso:brainstorm dispatch with one end-state SC ("the system supports OAuth") and one transitional SC ("OAuth migration is complete") routes the transitional SC to "## Closure Checks". A /dso:completion-verifier dispatch on an epic with one unresolved Closure Check and all end-state items passing returns refused-closure with a finding naming the unresolved Closure Check.

- SC8: plugins/dso/scripts/audit-closure-checks-migration.sh header contains the verbatim sentence "use sparingly — for simple field renames, targeted grep + one-pass update is sufficient." AND the script name appears in the CLAUDE.md Quick Reference table. Verified by grep against both files.

- SC9: Closure Checks template description requires each item to be one-shot verifiable (a command, a state check, or a reference to a specific named artifact). Standalone synthetic test: a /dso:brainstorm dispatch where a proposed Closure Check phrased as "team has reviewed the design" is submitted produces a rejection message referencing the one-shot-verifiable requirement.

- SC10: Multi-opus-agent workflow coherence walk-through gated between Phase 3 (audit and pointer updates complete) and Phase 4 (migration). Six parallel chunks, each opus-tier, each producing structured JSON {workflow_stage, status: PASS|AMBIGUOUS|FAIL, evidence_citations: [<file>:<line>], findings: [...]}:
  - Chunk A (brainstorm): reads plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/ SKILL.md + phases/* + prompts/*; validates dialogue produces correct end-state vs Closure Checks separation; verifies the new verifiable-sc-check rule is enforced; verifies approval gate output is well-formed.
  - Chunk B (preplanning): reads plugins/dso/skills/preplanning/ SKILL.md + prompts/* + docs/reviewers/*; validates story decomposition preserves the SC/Closure Checks distinction at the story level; validates done-definitions inherit end-state-only semantics.
  - Chunk C (implementation-plan): reads plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/ SKILL.md + prompts/* + docs/reviewers/*; validates task decomposition produces AC + Closure Checks correctly.
  - Chunk D (sprint): reads plugins/dso/skills/sprint/ SKILL.md + prompts/* + the completion-verifier dispatch path; validates execution sub-agents consume the schema; verifies completion-verifier subtree walk integrates correctly with the sprint closure flow.
  - Chunk E (commit and review): reads plugins/dso/docs/workflows/COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md + REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md + all code-reviewer-*.md agents; validates review surfaces Closure Checks failures distinctly from end-state failures.
  - Chunk F (operational dry-run): runs completion-verifier in dry-run mode against the 10 most recently closed brainstorm:complete-tagged epics; per epic, records the count of items that would have been flagged as transitional under the new schema; documents as before/after evidence that the migration prevents future false-positive closures.

  Aggregated report attached to ticket. Any FAIL or AMBIGUOUS finding blocks Phase 4 migration until resolved (spec amendment, prompt fix, or explicit defer decision).

## Approach

Four sequential phases plus a coherence walk-through gate:

- Phase 1: SC1 + SC2 — templates and end-state-only rule.
- Phase 2: SC3 — verifier refactor with pluggable hook, recursive walk via parent_id, legacy compat.
- Phase 3: SC4 + SC5 + SC8 — combined audit script and pointer updates.
- Phase 3.5 (gate): SC10 — multi-opus coherence walk-through.
- Phase 4: SC6 — haiku migration of brainstorm:complete-tagged epics.

SC7 + SC9 (synthetic tests) ship in Phase 4 verifying end-to-end behavior. Each phase is independently mergeable. During rollout, a merge-window coordination protocol pauses concurrent edits to templates, verifiable-sc-check.md, and completion-verifier.md (communicated via team channels).

## Scenario Analysis (Blue Team surviving)

- Classifier misclassifies end-state with completion-language (critical/correctness): partially mitigated by SC2 examples + SC6 ranking-based escalation; residual edge cases in past-tense durable invariants explicitly addressed by SC2 accept examples.
- Rubber-stamping under batch volume fatigue (high/adoption): mitigated by SC6 25-item batch cap and per-item explicit acknowledge.
- Recursive walk fan-out via shared descendant (critical/runtime): mitigated by SC3(c) parent_id-only walk semantics.
- Hook contract drift between default and future validators (high/correctness): partially mitigated by SC3(e) contract_version field; residual semantic drift remains until d566 and 94ed wire their validators.
- Reconciliation pass thrash (medium/runtime): mitigated by SC4 max-5-iteration cap with RECONCILIATION_INCOMPLETE surfaced.
- Default validator masks future hook breakage (high/correctness): partially mitigated by SC3(e) contract_version; residual risk is by-design (permissive default for legacy compat).
- End-state rule false positives on past-tense architectural SCs (high/correctness): partially mitigated by SC2 accept examples; reviewer judgment remains.
- Migration audit comment lost on subsequent edits (medium/observability): unmitigated; deferred to ticket-system observability work.
- SC8 over-use of audit pattern (low/adoption): partially mitigated by SC8 verbatim "use sparingly" guidance in script header.

## Research Findings

The brainstorm session for d566-afa6 surveyed three independent streams (academic literature, open-source tooling, practitioner thought leaders) on the question of test quality at generation time. That research established the framing in which Closure Checks emerges as a structural prerequisite — the literature universally rules out coverage-based and shape-only signals; the strongest available test-quality signals require knowing what intent each test is supposed to verify, which requires a clean end-state-only intent vocabulary in the source artifacts. This epic delivers that vocabulary.

## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)

### State Lifecycle Owner Block — RETIRE owners (Probe-3 remediation)

CREATE / CONSUME / UPDATE owners for the pluggable end-state-item-validator hook (`contract_version=1`) and the new `## Closure Checks` template section are already named in SC1 / SC3e / SC9. The audit identified missing RETIRE owners. Resolving here:

| Variable | RETIRE owner |
|---|---|
| `contract_version=1` (pluggable end-state-item-validator hook contract) | N/A — versioned contract. v1 is retired only via formal version bump to v2 with a documented migration plan; v1 persists indefinitely for backward compatibility until all consumers have migrated. Mirrors the versioned-contract pattern used elsewhere in the project (e.g., 7f42 `contract_version` in intent-coverage-findings). |
| `## Closure Checks` template section format | Two-track retirement matching SC6 + SC10 design: (a) closed tickets retain their legacy "Closure Checks" prose as immutable historical record — no rewriting; (b) open tickets at SC6 migration time are re-emitted with the new schema by the migration script. Legacy prose is sunset for new writes only; historical reads remain intact. |

Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -n 'contract_version\|Versioning Policy' plugins/dso/docs/contracts/end-state-item-validator.md` (or equivalent hook contract doc shipped by SC3e) shows `contract_version=1` published with a "Versioning Policy" subsection naming the v2 migration trigger.
- The a03c epic description's Operational Constraints section (this section) explicitly documents the two-track retirement policy for the `## Closure Checks` template format.

Closes the audit's named gaps: contract_version v1 RETIRE = versioned (formal v2 migration); legacy Closure Checks RETIRE = two-track (closed retain, open re-emitted via SC6).
## Dependencies

None. a03c-d55e is the root prerequisite of the test creation calibration program. d566-afa6, 94ed-f55c, 411b-a047, 7f42-e41f, and 69e8-af39 all depend on this schema cleavage.

## Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2 of scrutiny pipeline): not triggered — sufficient context inherited from d566-afa6 brainstorm research dispatches.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 17 red-team scenarios surfaced; 9 surviving after blue-team filter.
- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 2 conflicts (d566, 94ed) resolved via SC3 pluggable hook contract; 2 considerations (7f42, 69e8) on downstream consumer epics; 1 ambiguity on shared-file concurrent edits, mitigated by Approach merge-window note; 1 benign (4911 pattern reuse).
- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal — modifies verifiable-sc-check.md, completion-verifier.md, brainstorm/preplanning/sprint workflows). Five risks identified, all folded into SC2 (litmus test phrasing), SC3 (hook contract, walk semantics), SC6 (categorical classifier output, ranking-based escalation).
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity (5, 4), Scope (4, 5, 5, 5), Value (5, 4). All dimensions >= 4. Value reviewer's one minor finding (operational before/after metric) folded into SC10 Chunk F.
- Scale context (Step 0): small-to-medium — project-internal ticket count, fixed ~40 file/script touchpoints.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 10 (>= 7 threshold) — would route to /dso:preplanning full mode if invoked; preplanning explicitly deferred this session.
- User-directed scope additions during brainstorm:
  - Migration scope limited to brainstorm:complete-tagged epics (other epics re-brainstorm naturally).
  - Verifier sequencing locked at pluggable interface (a03c framework; d566/94ed plug in later).
  - Audit methodology locked at combined pattern sweep + reverse-dependency enumeration.
  - All .md LLM-guidance files in audit scope (workflows, prompts, contracts, agents).
  - Multi-opus workflow coherence walk-through added as Phase 3.5 gate (SC10).

Future batches should cap at ~10-15 epics per background invocation, or run plan-mode in foreground in smaller chunks. Bug filed: see follow-up.
- **mktemp bug**: classifier helper script uses `mktemp /tmp/audit-comment.XXXXXX.json` and `/tmp/new-desc.XXXXXX.txt` patterns at lines 168-169. On macOS BSD mktemp, these do NOT substitute the X's because the X's are not at the end of the basename — they create literal files. The script's EXIT trap cleans them up on clean exit, but when a prior invocation gets SIGKILL'd (e.g., by the background-timeout), the literal files leak. Subsequent invocations then fail with "mkstemp failed on /tmp/audit-comment.XXXXXX.json: File exists". Workaround applied this batch: `rm -f /tmp/audit-comment.XXXXXX.json /tmp/new-desc.XXXXXX.txt` before each invocation. Bug filed: see follow-up.
